Leo Mason III''' (born April 3, 1994) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for [[Limoges CSP]] of the [[LNB Pro A]]. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[University of Kansas]], where he was the starting [[point guard]] for the [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Jayhawks]]. For the [[2016–17 Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball team|2016–17 season]], he was the consensus National Player of the Year {{cite news |last=Norlander |first=Matt |date=March 29, 2017 |title=Kansas' Frank Mason parlays consistency, efficiency into CBS Player of the Year honor |url=http://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/kansas-frank-mason-parlays-consistency-efficiency-into-cbs-player-of-the-year-honor/ |work=[[CBS Sports]] |location=[[New York City]], [[New York (state)|New York]] |access-date=April 10, 2017}}{{cite news |last=Bedore |first=Gary |date=April 2, 2017 |title=KU's Frank Mason adds to award haul with NABC player of year. |url=http://www.kansascity.com/sports/college/big-12/university-of-kansas/article142336589.html |work=[[The Kansas City Star]] |location=[[Kansas City, Missouri]] |access-date=April 3, 2017}} He was also a consensus All-American selection for his senior season at Kansas.[http://www.kansascity.com/sports/college/big-12/university-of-kansas/article141222033.html Kansas' Frank Mason III is AP Player of the Year, unanimous All-American Selection], Kansas City Star, March 28, 2017. Mason was selected 34th overall in the [[2017 NBA draft]] by the [[Sacramento Kings]], where he spent two seasons before signing with the [[Milwaukee Bucks]] as a free agent in July 2019. He signed with the [[Orlando Magic]] in February 2021. ==Early life== Mason grew up in [[Petersburg, Virginia]] and went to [[Petersburg High School (Virginia)|Petersburg High School]]. He scored 1,901 points in his four-year career at Petersburg, which is the second-highest scoring total in school history behind [[Naismith Memorial Basketball Hall of Fame|Hall of Famer]] [[Moses Malone]].{{cite web|title=Frank Mason III – 2013–14 Men's Basketball|url=http://www.kuathletics.com/roster.aspx?rp_id=5200|website=KU Athletics| date=July 9, 2013 |access-date=April 3, 2017}} Mason had originally signed to attend [[Towson University]] in [[Towson, Maryland]] during his senior year, but he lost his eligibility after failing a government class.{{cite web|last1=Shaffer|first1=Jonas|title=A failing grade kept Kansas point guard Frank Mason III away from Towson|url=https://www.baltimoresun.com/2016/03/24/a-failing-grade-kept-kansas-point-guard-frank-mason-iii-away-from-towson/|website=The Baltimore Sun|access-date=March 21, 2017|archive-date=March 22, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170322112015/http://www.baltimoresun.com/sports/baltimore-sports-blog/bal-a-failing-grade-kept-kansas-point-guard-frank-mason-iii-away-from-towson-20160324-story.html|url-status=live}} Mason attended [[Massanutten Military Academy]] in [[Woodstock, Virginia]] to make up for the failing grade in government. After being discovered playing the [[Amateur Athletic Union]] circuit by Kansas Assistant Coach [[Kurtis Townsend]], Mason was offered a scholarship by the [[University of Kansas]].{{cite web|last1=Moore|first1=C.J.|title=HOW FRANK MASON WENT FROM UNWANTED RECRUIT TO THE KANSAS JAYHAWKS' LEADING MAN|url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2382892-how-frank-mason-went-from-unwanted-recruit-to-the-kansas-jayhawks-leading-man|website=Bleacher Report|access-date=March 21, 2017}} ==College career== [[File:Frank Mason vs. Florida.jpg|thumb|right|Mason makes a pass during a 2013 game]] As a sophomore at Kansas, he was a second team All Big 12 selection.{{cite web|title=Sooners' Hield Leads All-Big 12 Men's Basketball Honors|url=http://www.big12sports.com/ViewArticle.dbml?ATCLID=209934691|website=[[Big 12 Conference]]|access-date=May 17, 2015|date=March 8, 2015}} He averaged 12.6 points, 3.9 rebounds, and 3.9 assists per game as a sophomore, an increase from the 5.5 points, 1.3 rebounds, and 2.1 assists per game he averaged as a freshman.{{cite web|title=Frank Mason III|url=http://www.foxsports.com/college-basketball/frank-mason-player|website=[[Fox Sports]]|access-date=August 10, 2015}} During his junior season, Mason averaged 12.9 points and 4.6 assists and was named to the Big 12 All-Defensive Team. His regular season culminated in receiving multiple awards. He was unanimously selected as the Big 12 Player of the Year, averaging 20.5 points and 5.1 assists in the regular season.{{cite web|title=KU's Frank Mason, Bill Self are Big 12 player, coach of the year|url=http://www.kansascity.com/sports/college/big-12/university-of-kansas/article136592088.html|website=[[The Kansas City Star]]|access-date=March 21, 2017}} He was also consensus first team All-American selection, the NCAA-leading 29th first-team selection in Kansas basketball history.{{cite web|title=Mason earns Consensus All-America First Team distinction|url=http://www.kuathletics.com/news/2017/3/28/mens-basketball-mason-earns-consensus-all-america-first-team-distinction.aspx|website=KUAthletics.com|date=March 28, 2017 }} He was the first (2017–2019)=== Mason was drafted by the [[Sacramento Kings]] with the 34th pick in the [[2017 NBA draft]].{{cite news|title=Frank Mason III drafted in second round by Sacramento Kings|url=http://www.richmondfreepress.com/news/2017/jun/30/frank-mason-iii-drafted-second-round-sacramento-ki/|access-date=July 6, 2017|work=Richmond Free Press|date=June 30, 2017}} He played in the [[NBA Summer League]] for the Kings, where he scored 24 points in 24 minutes against the [[Los Angeles Lakers]] on July 10, 2017, adding 6 assists, 5 rebounds and 2 steals.Bisel, Tim. [http://cjonline.com/blog/tim-bisel/2017-07-11/summer-league-shootaround-frank-mason-heats-third-game Summer league shootaround: Frank Mason heats up in third game], ''[[Topeka Capitol-Journal]]'', July 11, 2017. For the full [[2017–18 NBA season|2017–18]] regular NBA season, Mason averaged 7.9 points, 2.5 rebounds and 2.8 assists in 52 games.Jones, Jason. [https://www.sacbee.com/sports/nba/sacramento-kings/kings-blog/article208538174.html Why the season is already over for Kings rookie Frank Mason III], [[Sacramento Bee]], April 10, 2018. Mason was waived by the Kings on July 4, 2019.{{cite news|title=Kings Waive Frank Mason III|url=https://www.nba.com/kings/blog/kings-waive-frank-mason-iii|access-date=July 4, 2019|work=NBA.com|date=July 4, 2019}} ===Milwaukee Bucks (2019–2020)=== Mason signed a [[two-way contract]] with the [[Milwaukee Bucks]] on July 26, 2019. In the deal, he split time between the Bucks and their [[NBA G League]] affiliate, the [[Wisconsin Herd]].{{cite news|title=Bucks Sign Frank Mason III and Cam Reynolds to Two-Way Contracts|url=https://www.nba.com/bucks/news/bucks-sign-frank-mason-iii-and-cam-reynolds-two-way-contracts|access-date=July 27, 2019|work=NBA.com|date=July 26, 2019}} In the G League, he scored 44 points in a win over the [[Grand Rapids Drive]] on February 19, 2020.{{cite news |title=Bucks' Frank Mason: Erupts in G League |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/bucks-frank-mason-erupts-in-g-league/ |access-date=February 20, 2020 |work=[[CBS Sports]] |date=February 20, 2020}} Mason was awarded the NBA G League MVP for the 2019–20 season on June 25, 2020. He averaged 26.4 points, 5.0 assists and 3.4 rebounds per game with the Herd.{{cite web|title=Wisconsin Herd's Frank Mason III Named 2019–20 NBA G League Most Valuable Player|url=https://www.nba.com/bucks/news/wisconsin-herds-frank-mason-iii-named-2019-20-nba-g-league-most-valuable-player|access-date=June 25, 2020|work=Milwaukee Bucks}} ===Orlando Magic (2021)=== On December 18, 2020, Mason signed with the [[Philadelphia 76ers]], but was waived the next day{{Cite tweet|number=1340344707185053701|user=LaurenMRosen|title=Official @sixers update|author=Lauren Rosen|date=December 19, 2020|access-date=March 1, 2021}} and signed with their [[NBA G League]] affiliate, the [[Delaware Blue Coats]].{{cite web|title=Blue Coats Announce 2021 Roster|url=https://bluecoats.gleague.nba.com/news/blue-coats-announce-2021-roster/|access-date=January 14, 2021|website=NBA.com}} However, on February 3, 2021, the [[Orlando Magic]] signed him to a [[two-way contract]] right before the beginning of the G League season.{{cite web|title=Orlando Magic Sign Free Agent Frank Mason III to Two-Way Contract Orlando waives Jordan Bone|url=https://www.nba.com/magic/orlando-magic-sign-free-agent-frank-mason-two-way-contract-20210203|website=NBA.com|date=February 3, 2021|access-date=February 3, 2021}} However, Mason was waived on February 15 after playing in four games.{{cite web|title=Magic's Frank Mason: Inks two-way deal with Magic|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/magics-frank-mason-inks-two-way-deal-with-magic/|access-date=February 3, 2021|website=CBSSports.com|date=February 3, 2021 }} Two days later, he was re-acquired by Delaware, but was waived on March 5 after suffering a season-ending injury. He didn't log any minutes with the Blue Coats.{{cite web|title=NBA G League Transactions|url=https://gleague.nba.com/transactions/|date=February 21, 2021|website=NBA.com|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210306044025/https://gleague.nba.com/transactions/|access-date=March 5, 2021|archive-date=March 6, 2021}} ===South Bay Lakers (2021–2022)=== Mason joined the [[Philadelphia 76ers]] for the [[2021 NBA Summer League]].{{Cite web |title=Philadelphia 76ers 2021 MGM Resorts NBA Summer League Roster |url=https://www.nba.com/summer-league/2021/vegas/team/1610612755/sixers |access-date=April 17, 2022 |website=NBA}} On October 13, 2021, Mason signed with the [[Los Angeles Lakers]]{{cite web|title=Lakers Sign Chaundee Brown Jr. and Mac McClung|url=https://www.nba.com/lakers/releases/lakers-sign-chaundee-brown-jr-and-mac-mcclung-2021|website=NBA.com|date=August 10, 2021|access-date=August 23, 2021}} and was waived the following day.{{cite web|title=Lakers Make Training Camp Cuts|url=https://www.nba.com/lakers/releases/lakers-make-training-camp-cuts-211015|website=NBA.com|date=October 15, 2021|access-date=October 23, 2021}} On October 23, he signed with the [[South Bay Lakers]] as an affiliate player.{{cite web|first=Nick|last=Kioski|title=South Bay Finalizes Training Camp Roster|url=https://southbay.gleague.nba.com/news/south-bay-finalizes-training-camp-roster/|website=NBA.com|date=October 23, 2021|access-date=October 23, 2021}} In seven games, he averaged 9.1 points, 3.0 rebounds and 3.3 assists per game.{{cite news |title=Herd acquire Frank Mason in a trade |url=https://fox11online.com/sports/bucks-and-nba/herd-acquire-frank-mason-in-a-trade |access-date=February 26, 2022 |work=Fox 11 News |date=February 24, 2022}} ===Wisconsin Herd (2022)=== On February 24, 2022, Mason was traded, along with a 2022 first-round pick, to the [[Wisconsin Herd]] in exchange for [[Tremont Waters]] and a 2022 second-round pick. In November 2022, he signed with [[Beirut Club]] of the [[Lebanese Basketball League]].{{cite web |last1=De Roa |first1=Alberto |title=Former Kings player Frank Mason signed with Lebanese team Beirut Club for the 2022-23 season. |url=https://hoopshype.com/rumor/1806708/ |publisher=HoopsHype |access-date=October 7, 2024 |date=November 21, 2022}} ===SLUC Nancy (2023–2024)=== On January 15, 2023,
